text: Rahu Kaal is one eighth of the daytime, chosen by the weekday (Monday 2nd, Saturday 3rd, Friday 4th, Wednesday 5th, Thursday 6th, Tuesday 7th, Sunday 8th part); new beginnings are avoided in it.
Yamaganda is one eighth of the daytime fixed by the weekday (Sunday 5th, Monday 4th, Tuesday 3rd, Wednesday 2nd, Thursday 1st, Friday 7th, Saturday 6th part) and is left out when choosing a time.

Gulika (Mandi) is Saturn's eighth of the daytime, counted from the weekday lord (Sunday 7th, Monday 6th, Tuesday 5th, Wednesday 4th, Thursday 3rd, Friday 2nd, Saturday 1st part), and is avoided for starting work.
Abhijit is the 8th of the 15 daytime muhurtas, the 48 minutes centred on local noon, and is counted as favourable on every weekday in this app (some almanacs omit Wednesdays).
Brahma muhurta is the second-last muhurta of the night, from 96 to 48 minutes before the next sunrise, kept for study and quiet practice.
Amrit choghadiya is the Moon's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as favourable.
Shubh choghadiya is Jupiter's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as favourable.
Labh choghadiya is Mercury's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as favourable.
Chal choghadiya is Venus's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as neutral.
Rog choghadiya is Mars's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and is avoided for starting work.
Kaal choghadiya is Saturn's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and is avoided for starting work.
Udveg choghadiya is the Sun's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and is avoided for starting work.
Each hora is one twelfth of the day or of the night, ruled in turn by Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter and Mars starting from the weekday lord at sunrise.

Bhadra is the Vishti karana, the first half of Shukla 8 and 15 and Krishna 7 and 14 and the second half of Shukla 4 and 11 and Krishna 3 and 10; it matters on earth only when the Moon is in Mesha, Vrishabha, Mithuna or Vrishchika, and new beginnings are then deferred.

Panchak runs while the Moon travels the last 300 to 360 degrees of the zodiac (Dhanishtha second half to Revati), when five kinds of work, such as roofing, bedding, travel south and cremation, are traditionally not begun.
Disha Shool names one direction per weekday in which a journey is not begun: east on Monday and Saturday, north on Tuesday and Wednesday, south on Thursday, west on Sunday and Friday.
Chandra bala counts the house of today's Moon from your birth Moon: the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th are favourable, the others are not, and the 8th is Chandrashtama.
The Moon returns to your birth sign today (1st from the natal Moon), a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 2nd sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 3rd sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 4th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 5th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 6th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 7th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 8th sign from your birth Moon today (Chandrashtama), the house Chandra bala sets aside; routine work continues, new starts wait for the Moon to move on.
The Moon is in the 9th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 10th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 11th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 12th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
Chandrashtama is the roughly two and a quarter days each month when the transiting Moon is in the 8th sign from your birth Moon; it is a day for routine, not for launches.

Tara bala counts from your birth nakshatra to today's nakshatra in cycles of nine: Sampat (2), Kshema (4), Sadhana (6), Mitra (8) and Parama Mitra (9) are favourable; Janma (1), Vipat (3), Pratyak (5) and Naidhana (7) are not.
Today's nakshatra is your Janma tara (1st of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is treated as neutral to unfavourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Sampat tara (2nd of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Vipat tara (3rd of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is not favourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Kshema tara (4th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Pratyak tara (5th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is not favourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Sadhana tara (6th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Naidhana tara (7th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is not favourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Mitra tara (8th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Parama Mitra tara (9th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
The day's tithi, nakshatra, yoga and weekday are read together from the Moon and Sun at sunrise, with Bhadra and Panchak noted as flags; special yogas arise from fixed weekday and nakshatra pairs.
Sade Sati is Saturn's transit through the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from your birth Moon, about seven and a half years in three phases; Dhaiya is Saturn's two and a half years in the 4th or 8th sign.
Phase 1 of Sade Sati: Saturn is in the 12th sign from your birth Moon, the opening two and a half years of the transit.
Phase 2 of Sade Sati: Saturn is in the same sign as your birth Moon, the middle two and a half years of the transit.
Phase 3 of Sade Sati: Saturn is in the 2nd sign from your birth Moon, the closing two and a half years of the transit.
Saturn is currently neither in the 12th, 1st, 2nd, 4th nor 8th sign from your birth Moon, so no Sade Sati or Dhaiya applies; the next one starts when Saturn enters such a sign.
Kantaka Dhaiya: Saturn is in the 4th sign from your birth Moon for about two and a half years.
Ashtama Dhaiya: Saturn is in the 8th sign from your birth Moon for about two and a half years.
The running Vimshottari mahadasha and antardasha lords are compared with today's weekday lord by Parashara's natural friendships, and their horas of the day are listed.
For each family member the same Chandra bala (Moon house from the birth Moon) and Tara bala (nakshatra count from the birth nakshatra) are computed from their own chart.
A planet is exalted (uchcha) in one fixed sign: Sun in Mesha, Moon in Vrishabha, Mars in Makara, Mercury in Kanya, Jupiter in Karka, Venus in Meena, Saturn in Tula.
A planet is debilitated (neecha) in the sign opposite its exaltation: Sun in Tula, Moon in Vrishchika, Mars in Karka, Mercury in Meena, Jupiter in Makara, Venus in Kanya, Saturn in Mesha.
A planet is in its own sign (swakshetra) when it rules the sign it occupies; moolatrikona is folded into this tag.
A planet is in a friend's sign when the sign's lord is its natural friend in Parashara's table of friendships.
A planet is in an enemy's sign when the sign's lord is its natural enemy in Parashara's table of friendships.
A planet is in a neutral sign when the sign's lord is neither friend nor enemy in Parashara's table of friendships.
A planet is combust (asta) when it lies within its orb of the Sun: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° retrograde), Saturn 15°.
A planet is retrograde (vakri) when its longitude decreases from day to day as seen from Earth; the Sun and Moon never are, Rahu and Ketu almost always are.
A planet is vargottama when it occupies the same sign in the D1 Rashi chart and the D9 Navamsa.
Vargottama means the D1 and D9 signs coincide, which happens in the first navamsa of a movable sign, the fifth of a fixed sign and the ninth of a dual sign.
Combustion orbs used: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° when retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° when retrograde), Saturn 15°; Rahu and Ketu are never combust.
This value carries approx. because the birth time was entered as approximate and shifting it by the stated minutes would move the value across a sign or house boundary.
This value carries approx. because the body lies within 1° of a sign boundary, where small differences in ayanamsa or time would change its sign.
With the birth time unknown the Lagna cannot be computed, so the Moon sign is placed in house 1 and houses are counted from it; dashas stay valid because they depend only on the Moon.
The Lagna is the sidereal sign rising on the eastern horizon at the birth time and place; it moves one sign roughly every two hours, so the chart is only as exact as the recorded time.

In whole-sign houses each house is one full sign counted from the Lagna, and its lord is the ruler of that sign: Mars (Mesha, Vrishchika), Venus (Vrishabha, Tula), Mercury (Mithuna, Kanya), Moon (Karka), Sun (Simha), Jupiter (Dhanu, Meena), Saturn (Makara, Kumbha).

Vimshottari dasha runs 120 years in the order Ketu 7, Venus 20, Sun 6, Moon 10, Mars 7, Rahu 18, Jupiter 16, Saturn 19, Mercury 17, starting from the lord of the birth nakshatra with a balance proportional to how much of it the Moon had still to cross.
A dasha change is the exact instant a maha, antar or pratyantar period ends, computed with a dasha year of 365.2425 days from the birth moment.
The janma tithi is the lunar month, paksha and tithi at the moment of birth; its anniversary is the day on which that tithi prevails at sunrise (udaya), skipping an Adhik month.
The barsi is the yearly shraddha on the tithi of passing, taken on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna); the same tithi number gives the Pitru Paksha day.
Pitru Paksha is the dark fortnight of Bhadrapada (Purnimanta Ashwin), from Purnima shraddha to Sarva Pitru Amavasya, each day matched to a tithi by the afternoon (aparahna) rule.
When the lunar month repeats as an Adhik month, recurring observances fall in the nija (regular) month of the same name, not in the Adhik one.
When a tithi begins after one sunrise and ends before the next (kshaya), it touches no sunrise, so the observance is kept on the day it begins.
Saturn's sign entry is the exact moment its sidereal longitude crosses a sign boundary, found by search, including retrograde re-entries.
Jupiter's sign entry is the exact moment its sidereal longitude crosses a sign boundary, found by search, including retrograde re-entries.
Rahu's sign entry is the moment the lunar node's sidereal longitude (mean node by default) crosses a sign boundary moving backwards; Ketu enters the opposite sign at the same time.

Ekadashi is kept on the day whose sunrise has the eleventh tithi (Smarta), or on the next day for Vaishnavas when Dashami still runs at dawn; parana follows the end of Hari Vasara within the Dwadashi, before a fifth of the day has passed.
Pradosh is the day the thirteenth tithi prevails at pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night after sunset, and is named by its weekday (Soma, Bhauma, Shani Pradosh).
Sankashti Chaturthi is the Krishna fourth tithi on the day it covers moonrise; on a Tuesday it is Angaraki.
Vinayaka Chaturthi is the Shukla fourth tithi on the day it covers midday (madhyahna).
Masik Shivaratri is the Krishna fourteenth tithi on the night it covers midnight (nishita).
The Purnima vrat is kept on the day the full-moon tithi prevails at moonrise, when the fast is broken.
Amavasya observances are kept on the day the new-moon tithi prevails at sunrise.
Karwa Chauth is Kartik Krishna Chaturthi on the day it covers moonrise; the fast runs from sunrise to that moonrise.
Chhath is Kartik Shukla Shashthi at sunrise, with Nahay Khay on Chaturthi, Kharna on Panchami, the evening arghya at sunset on Shashthi and the morning arghya at the next sunrise.
Hariyali Teej is Shravana Shukla Tritiya, Kajari Teej Bhadrapada Krishna Tritiya and Hartalika Teej Bhadrapada Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta names), each on the day whose sunrise has the tithi.
Navratri runs the nine days from Pratipada in Chaitra or Ashwin Shukla paksha; Ghatasthapana is done in the Pratipada while it runs after sunrise, or in Abhijit when it ends early.
The Satyanarayan vrat is kept on the Purnima day whose evening (sunset) still has the full-moon tithi, otherwise on the day it is at sunrise.
Makar Sankranti is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Makara (Makara sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Pongal (Thai Pongal) (observed in the south) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Makara (Makara sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Lohri (observed in the north) is 1 day before Makar Sankranti.
Thaipusam (observed in the south) is the day in the solar month of Makara whose sunrise has Pushya nakshatra; when two days qualify, the one with more daylight under that nakshatra is taken.
Vasant Panchami (Saraswati Puja) falls on Magha Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the forenoon (purvahna).
Ratha Saptami falls on Magha Shukla Saptami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Bhishma Ashtami falls on Magha Shukla Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), taking the day on which the tithi covers more of that period when it touches it on two days.

Jaya Ekadashi falls on Magha Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Magha Purnima falls on Magha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Mauni Amavasya falls on Magha Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Shattila Ekadashi falls on Magha Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Vijaya Ekadashi falls on Phalguna Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Maha Shivaratri falls on Phalguna Krishna Chaturdashi (Purnimanta month name), on the night that tithi covers midnight (nishita).

Amalaki Ekadashi falls on Phalguna Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Holika Dahan falls on Phalguna Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days, and the observance moves past any Bhadra (Vishti karana) that overlaps the window.
Holi (Dhulandi) is 1 day after Holika Dahan.
Rang Panchami (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Krishna Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Sheetala Ashtami (Basoda) (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Papmochani Ekadashi falls on Chaitra Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Ugadi (Telugu/Kannada New Year) (observed in the south) falls on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Gudi Padwa (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Chaitra Navratri runs from Chaitra Shukla Pratipada to Navami (Purnimanta month name), each day taken by the tithi at sunrise, so the span can be eight or ten days when a tithi is lost or repeated.
Gangaur (Gauri Tritiya) (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Rama Navami falls on Chaitra Shukla Navami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), taking the day on which the tithi covers more of that period when it touches it on two days.

Kamada Ekadashi falls on Chaitra Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Mahavir Jayanti falls on Chaitra Shukla Trayodashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Hanuman Jayanti (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Hanuman Jayanti (Tamil, Margazhi Amavasya) (observed in the south) falls on Pausha Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Chaitra Purnima falls on Chaitra Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Baisakhi (observed in the north) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Mesha (Mesha sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Vishu (observed in the south) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Mesha (Mesha sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Puthandu (Tamil New Year) (observed in the south) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Mesha (Mesha sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Akshaya Tritiya falls on Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, provided it runs at least 3 muhurtas after that sunrise (else the day before).
Parashurama Jayanti falls on Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).

Ganga Saptami (observed in the north) falls on Vaishakha Shukla Saptami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), taking the day on which the tithi covers more of that period when it touches it on two days.

Buddha Purnima falls on Vaishakha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Vat Savitri Vrat (observed in the north) falls on Jyeshtha Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Vat Purnima Vrat (observed in the south) falls on Jyeshtha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).
Ganga Dussehra (observed in the north) falls on Jyeshtha Shukla Dashami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Snana Purnima (Jagannath) falls on Jyeshtha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Guru Purnima falls on Ashadha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Kamika Ekadashi falls on Shravana Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Nag Panchami falls on Shravana Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Varalakshmi Vratam (observed in the south) is the last Friday before Shravana Shukla Purnima.

Raksha Bandhan falls on Shravana Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna), and the observance moves past any Bhadra (Vishti karana) that overlaps the window.
Kajari Teej (observed in the north) falls on Bhadrapada Krishna Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Hal Shashthi (Lalahi Chhath) (observed in the north) falls on Bhadrapada Krishna Shashthi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Radha Ashtami falls on Bhadrapada Shukla Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.

Onam (Thiruvonam) (observed in the south) is the day in the solar month of Simha whose sunrise has Shravana nakshatra; when two days qualify, the one with more daylight under that nakshatra is taken.

Pitru Paksha begins (Purnima Shraddha) is the Purnima shraddha that opens the dark fortnight of Bhadrapada (Purnimanta Ashwin); each following day is matched to a tithi by the afternoon (aparahna) rule down to Sarva Pitru Amavasya.
Jivitputrika (Jitiya) (observed in the north) falls on Ashwin Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Sarva Pitru Amavasya (Mahalaya) falls on Ashwin Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna).
Sharad Navratri runs from Ashwin Shukla Pratipada to Navami (Purnimanta month name), each day taken by the tithi at sunrise, so the span can be eight or ten days when a tithi is lost or repeated.
Durga Ashtami falls on Ashwin Shukla Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Maha Navami is 1 day before Dussehra (Vijaya Dashami).
Dussehra (Vijaya Dashami) falls on Ashwin Shukla Dashami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna).

Papankusha Ekadashi falls on Ashwin Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Sharad Purnima (Kojagari) falls on Ashwin Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the night that tithi covers midnight (nishita).
Karwa Chauth (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Krishna Chaturthi (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers moonrise.
Ahoi Ashtami (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).

Rama Ekadashi falls on Kartik Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Dhanteras falls on Kartik Krishna Trayodashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.
Naraka Chaturdashi (Kali Chaudas) falls on Kartik Krishna Chaturdashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Diwali (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Kartik Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.
Govardhan Puja (Annakut) falls on Kartik Shukla Pratipada (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Bhai Dooj falls on Kartik Shukla Dwitiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.
Labh Panchami (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Gopashtami falls on Kartik Shukla Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Akshaya Navami (Amla Navami) falls on Kartik Shukla Navami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Tulsi Vivah falls on Kartik Shukla Dwadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Kartik Purnima (Dev Deepawali) falls on Kartik Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Karthigai Deepam (observed in the south) is the day in the solar month of Vrishchika whose sunset falls in Krittika nakshatra (the lamps are lit at dusk); when no sunset falls in it, the day with more daylight under that nakshatra is taken.
Kalabhairav Jayanti falls on Margashirsha Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the night that tithi covers midnight (nishita).

Utpanna Ekadashi falls on Margashirsha Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Vivah Panchami falls on Margashirsha Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
